text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
- Cabinet agrees to new legislation for nuclear power and plans to lower subsidies to coal industry gradually over the next decade.

- Cabinet approves Research Minister Juergen Ruettgers plans for space exploration. Germany has invested 30 billion marks since the middle of the 1970s on space research and technology. Ruettgers wants to raise annual spending to two billion marks.
- Four out of 10 east German companies in the red, the Bundesbank says in a report.
- Bonn expected to remain the paymaster for EU. German demands to change EU financial system runs into deaf ear in Brussels. Bonn will thus remain by far the largest net contributor to EU budget.
- Minimum wage for construction workers will be cut from September.
- Post Minister Wolfgang Boetsch wants to force Deutsche Telekom to open access to its competitors.
- Lower Saxony premier Gerhard Schroeder urges SPD to make campaign pledge to work for coalition with environmentalist Greens party.
- Cabinet agrees to new nuclear energy plan. Government braces for resistance from opposition parties and states. Dispute focuses on nuclear dump sites.
- German managers unsatisfied with Bonn. Managers say the work of the coalition is as weak as never before.
